newsitem.title: ITALY: A Pope's day in hospital.
newsitem.headline: A Pope's day in hospital.

text.p: The world's eyes were on Pope John Paul on Tuesday when he had an operation to remove his appendix.
Following is a reconstruction of his day based on statements by chief Vatican spokesman Joaquin Navarro-Valls and doctors who carried out what one of them called a "textbook" operation.

3 a.m. - The Pope wakes and retires to the chapel in his special suite at the Gemelli Hospital for two hours of solitary prayer. Navarro-Valls says the Pontiff said "mental prayers", read from his prayer book and recited part of the rosary.
5 a.m. - The Pope celebrates mass led by his personal secretary, Monsignor Stanislaw Dziwisz. Afterwards he returns to his room to prepare for surgery.
7:00 a.m. - The Pope is taken to the operating theatre.
9:30 a.m. - Doctors and guards return the Pope to his suite.

"He started to regain consciousness as he was being taken back to his room and was fully conscious when he arrived there. He asked the doctors how it went," Navarro-Valls says. The Pope asks to hear the medical bulletin to be released later in the morning. A nun, who is one of his nurses, reads it aloud.
11:30 a.m. - As the Pope rests, Francesco Crucitti, chief surgeon at Gemelli, tells a packed news conference that the operation was a perfect success.
